Query and Query results

Two of the nineteen tab types and one surface. Drag the grips to resize: at 860 the composer leaves the editor's side, which is the one view specific width in the whole workbench and it is published, not mine. docs/adaptive-pane-ux.md: "Query already needs 860 pixels for its composer arrangement; preserve that requirement until testing supports a change."

What changed

BeforeNow
88 rules still in the original styles.css, the largest surviving block of pre convergence styling in the rendererBound to the shared layer. Nothing here declares a colour of its own
Query results is a grid with none of the column work Individuals receivedThe same column chooser model: each column carries fill and distinct, and a column that is derived, unique per row or empty says so
History and actions compete for bar widthOne action row. History is a popup anchored to its button, so it costs no band and no width

Branching, which the grid makes visible

docs/query-history-ux.md keeps query documents in a history that branches rather than truncating later entries. Running an edited query from a history entry creates a branch, and the history popup marks it. That is why the entries carry a parent rather than a flat timestamp.

Describe, the local agent composer

The second tab of the composer, and a Compose query action in the row. Type what you want, press Generate, and Axiom launches the Codex or Claude executable it found on PATH. This is not a new idea of mine: docs/sparql-agent-integration.md specifies it and records it as implemented, down to the versions exercised, so the shape here follows that document rather than inventing a second one.

One toggle covers create, augment and change. Refine the current query off sends your description plus the ontology context, which is a new query. On, the editor text joins the request, which is a revision. The published reason is worth keeping: "This distinction lets the same interaction support both a new query and a revision without making users learn separate modes."

The gate between the agent and your editor

The agent drafts text. Axiom owns the ontology context and the execution, and nothing reaches the editor without passing a check. Five of those checks are implemented here and you can trigger all of them from the description field:

Ask it to delete or insert somethingIt returns an update. Rejected: this panel never writes to the ontology
Ask about an instructorIt invents ax:Instructor. Rejected by name, because that term is not in the context Axiom sent. This is the check that catches a plausible looking identifier the ontology does not have
Ask about the weatherAnswered as unsupported, with the reason. No empty document is opened
Ask for credits or synonymsValidated and offered, with its explanation and assumptions beside it
Use the menu to sign the agent outGeneration fails with the diagnostic and a retry. Found on PATH proves an executable exists, never that an account, a model or a quota does

Also implemented, and harder to trigger by hand: more than one code block is rejected rather than picking one by position, and a projection that selects a variable the pattern never binds is named and refused. A proposal that fails validation is kept for correction rather than discarded, and Run stays unavailable until you change the text, which is why the state line says so rather than leaving a dead button.

Three things it deliberately does not do

It never runs anything. Generation and execution are separate in the code, not just in the layout, which is what makes the review boundary real rather than a request the assistant is trusted to honour.

It never asks for an API key. There is no field for one and there is no place to put one. The CLI uses its own terminal sign in. A missing provider is labelled and Refresh agents rescans PATH.

It does not hide what it sends. The disclosure carries the exact prompt, the ontology lines, the omitted count and the executable path, before you press Generate. Your query text is in there only when the refine toggle is on. The published limits are 160 ranked entities and 120 predicates; this ontology is well under both, so nothing is omitted and the counter says zero rather than nothing at all.

Where it goes when the pane narrows

Below 860 the composer has no side column, so Compose query gives it the body and generation returns you to the editor. That is the published behaviour for this view, and it is the reason the action sits in the row rather than only in the composer.

What runs and what does not

The evaluator is real but small: SELECT with a variable list, a basic graph pattern of triple patterns, one optional FILTER(CONTAINS(?var, "text")) and an optional LIMIT, joined by nested loops over a seeded store of 64 triples. Prefixes resolve. Anything outside that subset reports what it could not parse rather than returning an empty grid, because an empty grid and a rejected query are different facts.

Not implemented here: the SPARQL agent, update operations, endpoint selection and result export. Those are owned by docs/sparql-agent-integration.md and are behaviour rather than presentation.
